content:
Krail waits. The pen lies on the table beside the unsigned order, its nib capped, aligned with the paper's edge as though the document itself had been tidied into readiness. His grey eyes rest on you without hurry, giving you the same attention he would give a ledger line that refuses to balance.

When you do not reach for the pen, he straightens.

"Young lord." His voice stays level, dry as folded parchment. "There is no requirement that you decide this instant. The household does not run on the temper of its children, and I have ledgers, rosters, and a blocked delivery at the east gate that will not resolve themselves while I stand here."

He lifts the pen, caps it fully, and sets it down again — parallel to the order, half an inch from the paper's edge. A small ceremony of withholding. The punishment remains unauthorized, and he makes sure the geometry of the table says so.

"I will leave the order here." He taps the page once with two fingers. "Signed or unsigned, it does not leave this room without your mark. The girls remain in your custody. The physician in the east wing remains available, should you decide their burns concern you more than the estate's records do."

At the word *records*, something tightens almost invisibly at the corner of his mouth. It is gone before it can be called an expression.

"Consider, while I am gone, what a fire in Lady Ilyra's rooms costs this house. Not the furniture — furniture is replaceable. The register that burned was entered under my stewardship. Its loss will be entered against someone." He looks at Elise when he says it. "Whether that someone is the girl who struck the lamp, or the mother who lost her keys, or no one at all — that depends on what is written down tomorrow."

Elise's clasped hands whiten at the knuckles. Her bandaged forearm stays carefully still at her side, but her chin lifts a fraction, and her voice comes out steady despite the brown stain at the center of the wrapping. "I've told you where my keys were, Master Krail. I've told you twice."

"You have told me a story," Krail says. "Stories are not inventories." He gathers his cuffs, smooths them, and bows — precisely, shallowly, correctly — toward you and not toward the prisoners.

"Forgive the interruption of your morning, my lord. I will return before the midday bell for your answer." His polished shoes cross the floor without a sound of hurry. At the door he pauses, hand on the latch, and glances back once — not at you, but at the ruined portrait leaning against the wall, at the scorched curtains, at the smell of wet ash. Whatever he calculates from it, he keeps.

Then the door closes behind him, and the room is quieter than it has been all morning.

Liora is the first to move. She shifts her weight off her blistered palm, pressing it instead against her skirt, and stares at the unsigned order on the table as if it might bite. Her reddish-brown eyes flick from the paper to you, then to her mother, then down to the floor. She does not begin explaining this time. That, from Liora, is its own kind of speech.

Elise exhales slowly through her nose. "Thank you for hearing us, my lord," she says, and there is a careful gap in the sentence — a space where more could go, if you let it.

Isolde stands at your shoulder, hands folded, white hair still perfectly ordered. She turns her head a small degree toward you, yellow eyes waiting on your face. She says nothing. The bond requires her obedience, not her opinion, and she offers none unprompted.

The order sits on the table. The pen sits beside it. Midday is coming.
